title: High press
review_status: auxiliary source only; excluded from UEFA gold-standard answers
text: A high press depends on connected team structure from the goalkeeper to the forwards. Keep suitable distances between units so opponents cannot play through gaps. Use shared triggers and pressing traps to steer play toward chosen areas; the nearest player applies pressure while teammates cover likely options. Pressing intensity should fit the game state, and the high line requires an appropriately positioned goalkeeper.

title: Switch of play
review_status: auxiliary source only; excluded from UEFA gold-standard answers
text: A switch can exploit space after moving a compact opponent toward the ball. The passer needs time and space to deliver accurately; receivers on the far side should create separation and use the width of the pitch. Supporting players should anticipate the switch and run to help progress the attack or create a local overload. Check the opponent’s defensive organization before selecting this option.

title: The counter-attack
review_status: auxiliary source only; excluded from UEFA gold-standard answers
text: A counter-attack begins with regaining possession and uses the moment before the opponent reorganizes. Move the ball forward with purpose through a carry or direct pass, while teammates make immediate supporting runs, including runs that stretch the defensive line. Whether to counter depends on the space, support, and opportunity to progress; the final pass must match the developing advantage.

title: The reaction to losing the ball
review_status: auxiliary source only; excluded from UEFA gold-standard answers
text: After losing possession, the closest player may press immediately, while a collective counter-press requires teammates to close space and likely passing options together. Teams can use shared triggers and anticipate where the opponent will try to play. A coordinated press may force a poor pass or clearance even when it does not win the ball immediately. The choice depends on team organization, distances, fitness, and the available cover.
